sources: University of Kentucky Entomology, ENTFACT-609 Clothes Moths (M. F. Potter): "Clothes moth adults do not feed so they cause no injury to fabrics. However, the adults lay about 40-50 pinhead-sized eggs on vulnerable substrates, which in turn, hatch into the fabric-eating larvae."; "They feed exclusively on animal fibers, especially wool, fur, silk, feathers, felt, and leather."; "clothes moths are seldom seen because they avoid light. They prefer dark, undisturbed areas such as closets, basements and attics. Similar-looking moths spotted in kitchens and other well-lighted areas are possibly grain moths originating from cereals, dried fruit, nuts, or other stored foods."; https://entomology.ca.uky.edu/files/ef609.pdf

UC IPM Pest Notes: Clothes Moths: "The larva is the damaging stage of the clothes moth. Both species feed on wool clothing, carpets, and rugs; upholstered furniture; furs; stored woolen items..."; https://ipm.ucanr.edu/PMG/PESTNOTES/pn7435.html

UC IPM Pest Notes: Pantry Pests: "Stored-product pests are usually brought into the home in an infested package of food."; Indian meal moth: "All damage is done by the larvae, which attack a wide range of products including cereal and cereal products, flour, cornmeal, rice, dried fruit, dehydrated vegetables, nuts, chocolate, candies, and other confections."; https://ipm.ucanr.edu/home-and-landscape/pantry-pests/
